Since the 1940s, southern California has had a reputation for smog. Things are not as bad as they once were but, according to the American Lung Association, Los Angeles is still the worst city in the United States for levels of __26__ . Gazing down on the city from the Getty Center, an art museum in the Santa Monica Mountains, one would find the view of the Pacific Ocean blurred by the haze (霾). Nor is the state's bad air __27__ to its south. Fresno, in the central valley, comes top of the list in America for year-round pollution. Residents' hearts and lungs are affected as a __28__ . All of which, combined with California's reputation as the home of technological __29__ , makes the place ideal for developing and testing systems designed to monitor pollution in __30__ . And that is just what Aclima, a new firm in San Francisco, has been doing over the past few months. It has been trying out monitoring stations that are __31__ to yield minute-to-minute maps of __32__ air pollution. Such stations will also be able to keep an eye on what is happening inside buildings, including offices.
paragraphs.translationZh: 自 20 世纪 40 年代以来，南加州就因雾霾而闻名。情况并不像以前那么糟糕，但根据美国肺脏协会的数据，洛杉矶仍然是美国污染物水平最差的城市。从圣莫尼卡山脉的盖蒂中心（Getty Center）艺术博物馆俯瞰整座城市，太平洋的景色被雾霾所模糊。该州的恶劣空气也不仅限于南部。位于中部山谷的弗雷斯诺在美国全年污染情况中名列前茅。居民的心脏和肺部因此受到影响。所有这些，再加上加州作为技术创新之乡的声誉，使这里成为开发和测试旨在详细监测污染的系统的理想之地。这正是旧金山的一家新公司 Aclima 在过去几个月里一直在做的事情。它一直在尝试建立监测站，旨在生成每分钟的室外空气污染地图。此类站点还能够监视建筑物（包括办公室）内发生的情况。

paragraphs.sourceText: To this end, Aclima has been __33__ with Google's Street View system. Davida Herzl, Aclima's boss, says they have revealed pollution highs on days when San Francisco's transit workers went on strike and the city's __34__ were forced to use their cars. Conversely, "cycle to work" days have done their job by __35__ pollution lows.
paragraphs.translationZh: 为此，Aclima 一直与谷歌街景系统合作。 Aclima 的老板达维达·赫茨尔 (Davida Herzl) 表示，他们透露，旧金山交通工人罢工、该市居民被迫使用汽车时，污染严重。相反，“骑车上班”日通过降低污染水平发挥了作用。

paragraphs.sourceText: As Tourists Crowd Out Locals, Venice Faces 'Endangered' List
paragraphs.translationZh: 随着游客挤走当地人，威尼斯面临“濒危”名单

paragraphs.sourceText: A. On a recent fall morning, a large crowd blocked the steps at one of Venice's main tourist sites, the Rialto Bridge. The Rialto Bridge is one of the four bridges spanning the Grand Canal. It is the oldest bridge across the canal, and was the dividing line between the districts of San Marco and San Polo. But on this day, there was a twist: it was filled with Venetians, not tourists.
paragraphs.translationZh: 答：最近一个秋天的早晨，一大群人封锁了威尼斯主要旅游景点之一里亚托桥的台阶。里亚托桥是横跨大运河的四座桥梁之一。它是横跨运河的最古老的桥梁，也是圣马可区和圣波罗区之间的分界线。但这一天，出现了一个转折：这里挤满了威尼斯人，而不是游客。

paragraphs.sourceText: B. "People are cheering and holding their carts in the air," says Giovanni Giorgio, who helped organize the march with a grass-roots organization called Generazione '90. The carts he refers to are small shopping carts—the symbol of a true Venetian. "It started as a joke," he says with a laugh. "The idea was to put blades on the wheels! You know? Like Ben Hur. Precisely like that, you just go around and run people down."
paragraphs.translationZh: B. 乔瓦尼·乔治奥 (Giovanni Giorgio) 表示：“人们欢呼雀跃，并将手推车举在空中。”他与一个名为 Generazione '90 的草根组织一起帮助组织了这次游行。他所说的手推车是小型购物车——真正威尼斯人的象征。 “这开始只是一个笑话，”他笑着说。 “我们的想法是在轮子上装上刀片！你知道吗？就像《宾虚》一样。就像那样，你只是四处走动，把人撞倒。”

paragraphs.sourceText: C. Venice is one of the hottest tourist destinations in the world. But that's a problem. Up to 90,000 tourists crowd its streets and canals every day—far outnumbering the 55,000 permanent residents. The tourist increase is one key reason the city's population is down from 175,000 in the 1950s. The outnumbered Venetians have been steadily fleeing. And those who stick around are tired of living in a place where they can't even get to the market without swimming through a sea of picture-snapping tourists. Imagine, navigating through 50,000 people while on the way to school or to work.
paragraphs.translationZh: C. 威尼斯是世界上最热门的旅游目的地之一。但这是个问题。每天有多达 90,000 名游客涌入街道和运河，远远超过 55,000 名常住居民。游客的增加是该市人口从 20 世纪 50 年代的 175,000 人下降的主要原因之一。寡不敌众的威尼斯人一直在不断逃离。那些留下来的人厌倦了生活在这样一个地方：如果不穿过一大群拍照的游客，他们甚至无法到达市场。想象一下，在上学或上班的路上穿过 50,000 人。

paragraphs.sourceText: D. Laura Chigi, a grandmother at the march, says the local and national governments have failed to do anything about the crowds for decades, because they're only interested in tourism—the primary industry in Venice, worth more than $3 billion in 2015. "Venice is a cash cow," she says, "and everyone wants a piece."
paragraphs.translationZh: 参加游行的祖母 D. Laura Chigi 表示，几十年来，地方和国家政府对人群没有采取任何措施，因为他们只对旅游业感兴趣——旅游业是威尼斯的主要产业，2015 年价值超过 30 亿美元。“威尼斯是一棵摇钱树，”她说，“每个人都想分一杯羹。”

paragraphs.sourceText: E. Just beyond St. Mark's Square, a cruise ship passes, one of hundreds every year that appear over their medieval (中世纪的) surroundings. Their massive wake creates waves at the bottom of the sea, weakening the foundations of the centuries-old buildings themselves. "Every time I see a cruise ship, I feel sad," Chigi says. "You see the mud it drags; the destruction it leaves in its wake? That hurts the ancient wooden poles holding up the city underwater. One day we'll see Venice break down."
paragraphs.translationZh: E. 就在圣马可广场外，一艘游轮经过，这是每年数百艘游轮出现在中世纪周围地区的其中之一。它们巨大的尾流在海底产生波浪，削弱了具有数百年历史的建筑物本身的地基。 “每次看到游轮，我都会感到难过，”奇吉说。 “你看到它拖曳的泥土；它留下的破坏吗？这伤害了支撑水下城市的古老木杆。有一天我们会看到威尼斯崩溃。”

paragraphs.sourceText: F. For a time, UNESCO, the cultural wing of the United Nations, seemed to agree. Two years ago, it put Italy on notice, saying the government was not protecting Venice. UNESCO considers the entire city a World Heritage Site, a great honor that means Venice, at the cultural level, belongs to all of the world's people. In 2014, UNESCO gave Italy two years to manage Venice's flourishing tourism or the city would be placed on another list—World Heritage In Danger, joining such sites as Aleppo and Palmyra, destroyed by the war in Syria.
paragraphs.translationZh: F. 有一段时间，联合国教科文组织（联合国的文化部门）似乎也同意这一观点。两年前，它向意大利发出警告，称政府没有保护威尼斯。联合国教科文组织将整个城市列为世界遗产，这是一项巨大的荣誉，这意味着威尼斯在文化层面上属于全世界人民。 2014年，联合国教科文组织给了意大利两年的时间来管理威尼斯蓬勃发展的旅游业，否则这座城市将被列入另一个名单——濒危世界遗产，与被叙利亚战争摧毁的阿勒颇和巴尔米拉等遗址一起列入濒危世界遗产名单。

paragraphs.sourceText: G. Venice's deadline passed with barely a murmur (嘟哝) this summer, just as UNESCO was meeting in Istanbul. Only one representative, Jad Tabet from Lebanon, tried to raise the issue. "For several years, the situation of heritage in Venice has been worsening, and it has now reached a dramatic situation," Tabet told UNESCO. "We have to act quickly—there is not a moment to waste."
paragraphs.translationZh: 今年夏天，正当联合国教科文组织在伊斯坦布尔开会时，威尼斯的最后期限悄无声息地过去了。只有一位代表，来自黎巴嫩的贾德·塔贝特，试图提出这个问题。塔贝特告诉联合国教科文组织：“几年来，威尼斯的遗产状况一直在恶化，现在已经达到了戏剧性的地步。” “我们必须迅速采取行动——一刻也不能浪费。”

paragraphs.sourceText: H. But UNESCO didn't even hold a vote. "It's been postponed until 2017," says Anna Somers, the founder and CEO of The Art Newspaper and the former head of Venice in Peril, a group devoted to restoring Venetian art. She says the main reason the U.N. cultural organization didn't vote to declare Venice a World Heritage Site In Danger is because UNESCO has become
paragraphs.translationZh: H. 但联合国教科文组织甚至没有进行投票。 “它被推迟到 2017 年，”《艺术报》创始人兼首席执行官、致力于恢复威尼斯艺术的威尼斯危机组织前负责人安娜·萨默斯 (Anna Somers) 说道。她说联合国文化组织没有投票宣布威尼斯为濒危世界遗产的主要原因是因为联合国教科文组织已经

paragraphs.sourceText: "intensely politicized. There would have been some back-room negotiations."
paragraphs.translationZh: “政治化程度很高。可能会进行一些幕后谈判。”

paragraphs.sourceText: I. Italy boasts more UNESCO World Heritage Sites than any other country in the world, granting it considerable power and influence within the organization. The former head of the UNESCO World Heritage Centre, which oversees heritage sites, is Francesco Bandarin, a Venetian who now serves as UNESCO's assistant director-general for culture.
paragraphs.translationZh: 一、意大利拥有比世界上任何国家都多的联合国教科文组织世界遗产，赋予其在该组织内相当大的权力和影响力。负责管理遗产地的联合国教科文组织世界遗产中心前任负责人是威尼斯人弗朗切斯科·班达林 (Francesco Bandarin)，他现在担任联合国教科文组织负责文化事务的助理总干事。

paragraphs.sourceText: J. Earlier this year, Italy signed an accord with UNESCO to establish a task force of police art detectives and archaeologists (考古学家) to protect cultural heritage from natural disasters and terror groups, such as ISIS. The accord underlined Italy's global reputation as a good steward of art and culture.
paragraphs.translationZh: J. 今年早些时候，意大利与联合国教科文组织签署了一项协议，成立一个由警察艺术侦探和考古学家组成的特别工作组，以保护文化遗产免受自然灾害和伊斯兰国等恐怖组织的侵害。该协议凸显了意大利作为艺术和文化良好管理者的全球声誉。

paragraphs.sourceText: K. But adding Venice to the UNESCO endangered list—which is dominated by sites in developing and conflict-ridden countries—would be an international embarrassment, and could even hurt Italy's profitable tourism industry. The Italian Culture Ministry says it is unaware of any government efforts to pressure UNESCO. As for the organization itself, it declined a request for an interview.
paragraphs.translationZh: K. 但是，将威尼斯列入联合国教科文组织濒危名单（该名单主要由发展中国家和饱受冲突蹂躏的国家的遗址组成）将令国际社会感到尴尬，甚至可能损害意大利盈利的旅游业。意大利文化部表示，不知道政府有任何向联合国教科文组织施压的行为。至于该组织本身，它拒绝了采访请求。

paragraphs.sourceText: L. The city's current mayor, Luigi Brugnaro, has ridiculed UNESCO and told it to mind its own business, while continuing to support the cruise ship industry, which employs 5,000 Venice residents.
paragraphs.translationZh: L. 该市现任市长路易吉·布鲁尼亚罗 (Luigi Brugnaro) 嘲笑联合国教科文组织，并要求其管好自己的事，同时继续支持雇用 5,000 名威尼斯居民的游轮业。

paragraphs.sourceText: M. As for Venetians, they're beyond frustrated and hoping for a solution soon. "It's a nightmare for me. Some situations are really difficult with tourists around," says Giorgio as he navigates around a swelling crowd at the Rialto Bridge. "There are just so many of them. They never know where they are going, and do not walk in an orderly manner. Navigating the streets can be exhausting."
paragraphs.translationZh: M. 至于威尼斯人，他们非常沮丧，希望尽快找到解决方案。 “这对我来说是一场噩梦。周围有游客，有些情况真的很困难，”乔治在里亚托桥拥挤的人群中穿行时说道。 “他们太多了。他们永远不知道自己要去哪里，而且走路也不有序。在街上穿行会让人筋疲力尽。”

paragraphs.sourceText: N. Then it hits him: This crowd isn't made up of tourists. They're Venetians. Giorgio says he's never experienced the Rialto Bridge this way in all his 22 years. "For once, we are the ones who are blocking the traffic," he says delightedly. "It feels unreal. It feels like we're some form of endangered species. It's just nice. The feeling is just pure." But, he worries, if tourism isn't managed and his fellow locals continue to move to the mainland, his generation might be the last who can call themselves native Venetians.
paragraphs.translationZh: N. 然后他突然意识到：这群人并不是由游客组成的。他们是威尼斯人。 Giorgio 说，他 22 年来从未以这种方式体验过里亚托桥。 “这一次，我们成为了堵塞交通的人，”他高兴地说。 “这感觉很不真实。感觉就像我们是某种濒临灭绝的物种。这很好。这种感觉很纯粹。”但是，他担心，如果旅游业得不到管理，而他的当地人继续移居大陆，他这一代人可能是最后一个可以称自己为本土威尼斯人的人。

paragraphs.sourceText: 36. The passing cruise ships will undermine the foundations of the ancient buildings in Venice.
paragraphs.translationZh: 36. 过往的游轮会破坏威尼斯古建筑的地基。

paragraphs.sourceText: 37. The Italian government has just reached an agreement with UNESCO to take measures to protect its cultural heritage.
paragraphs.translationZh: 37. 意大利政府刚刚与教科文组织达成协议，采取措施保护其文化遗产。

paragraphs.sourceText: 38. The heritage situation in Venice has been deteriorating in the past few years.
paragraphs.translationZh: 38. 过去几年，威尼斯的遗产状况一直在恶化。

paragraphs.sourceText: 39. The decrease in the number of permanent residents in Venice is mainly due to the increase of tourists.
paragraphs.translationZh: 39. 威尼斯常住居民人数减少主要是由于游客增加。

paragraphs.sourceText: 40. If tourism gets out of control, native Venetians may desert the city altogether one day.
paragraphs.translationZh: 40. 如果旅游业失控，威尼斯本地人有一天可能会完全抛弃这座城市。

paragraphs.sourceText: 41. UNESCO urged the Italian government to undertake its responsibility to protect Venice.
paragraphs.translationZh: 41. 教科文组织敦促意大利政府承担起保护威尼斯的责任。

paragraphs.sourceText: 42. The participants in the Venetian march used shopping carts to show they were 100% local residents.
paragraphs.translationZh: 42. 威尼斯游行的参与者使用购物车来表明他们是100%的当地居民。

paragraphs.sourceText: 43. Ignoring UNESCO's warning, the mayor of Venice maintains his support of the city's tourism industry.
paragraphs.translationZh: 43. 威尼斯市长无视联合国教科文组织的警告，继续支持该市的旅游业。

paragraphs.sourceText: 44. One woman says that for decades the Italian government and local authorities have only focused on the revenues from tourism.
paragraphs.translationZh: 44. 一名妇女表示，几十年来意大利政府和地方当局只关注旅游业的收入。

paragraphs.sourceText: 45. UNESCO has not yet decided to put Venice on the list of World Heritage Sites In Danger.
paragraphs.translationZh: 45. 教科文组织尚未决定将威尼斯列入濒危世界遗产名录。

paragraphs.sourceText: Questions 46 to 50 are based on the following passage.
paragraphs.translationZh: 第 46 至 50 题基于以下段落。

paragraphs.sourceText: Living in an urban area with green spaces has a long-lasting positive impact on people's mental well-being, a study has suggested. UK researchers found moving to a green space had a sustained positive effect, unlike pay rises or promotions, which only provided a short-term boost. Co-author Mathew White, from the University of Exeter, UK, explained that the study showed people living in greener urban areas were displaying fewer signs of depression or anxiety. "There could be a number of reasons," he said, "for example, people do many things to make themselves happier: they strive for promotion or pay rises, or they get married. But the trouble with those things is that within six months to a year, people are back to their original baseline levels of well-being. So, these things are not sustainable; they don't make us happy in the long term. We found that for some lottery (彩票) winners who had won more than ￡500,000 the positive effect was definitely there, but after six months to a year, they were back to the baseline."
paragraphs.translationZh: 一项研究表明，生活在拥有绿色空间的城市地区对人们的心理健康具有长期的积极影响。英国研究人员发现，搬到绿色空间会产生持续的积极影响，这与加薪或晋升不同，后者只能提供短期的推动作用。来自英国埃克塞特大学的合著者马修·怀特解释说，这项研究表明，生活在绿色城市地区的人们表现出的抑郁或焦虑迹象较少。 “原因可能有很多，”他说，“例如，人们会做很多事情来让自己更快乐：他们争取升职或加薪，或者结婚。但这些事情的问题在于，在六个月到一年之内，人们就会回到原来的幸福基准水平。所以，这些事情是不可持续的；从长远来看，它们不会让我们快乐。我们发现，对于一些赢得超过50万英镑的积极影响肯定是存在的，但六个月到一年后，他们又回到了基线。”

paragraphs.sourceText: Dr. White said his team wanted to see whether living in greener urban areas had a lasting positive effect on people's sense of well-being or whether the effect also disappeared after a period of time. To do this, the team used data from the British Household Panel Survey compiled by the University of Essex.
paragraphs.translationZh: 怀特博士说，他的团队希望了解生活在绿色城市地区是否会对人们的幸福感产生持久的积极影响，或者这种影响在一段时间后是否也会消失。为此，该团队使用了埃塞克斯大学编制的英国家庭追踪调查的数据。

paragraphs.sourceText: Explaining what the data revealed, he said: "What you see is that even after three years, mental health is still better, which is unlike many other things that we think will make us happy." He observed that people living in green spaces were less stressed, and less stressed people made more sensible decisions and communicated better.
paragraphs.translationZh: 在解释数据显示的内容时，他说：“你看到的是，即使三年后，心理健康状况仍然更好，这与我们认为会让我们快乐的许多其他事情不同。”他观察到，生活在绿色空间的人们压力较小，而压力较小的人会做出更明智的决定并更好地沟通。

paragraphs.sourceText: With a growing body of evidence establishing a link between urban green spaces and a positive impact on human well-being, Dr. White said, "There's growing interest among public policy officials, but the trouble is who funds it. What we really need at a policy level is to decide where the money will come from to help support good quality local green spaces."
paragraphs.translationZh: 怀特博士说，随着越来越多的证据表明城市绿色空间与对人类福祉的积极影响之间存在联系，“公共政策官员的兴趣越来越大，但问题是谁提供资金。我们在政策层面真正需要的是决定资金从哪里来，以帮助支持优质的当地绿色空间。”

paragraphs.sourceText: You probably know about the Titanic, but it was actually just one of three state-of-the-art (先进的) ocean ships back in the day. The Olympic class ships were built by the Harland & Wolff ship makers in Northern Ireland for the White Star Line company. The Olympic class included the Olympic, the Britannic and the Titanic. What you may not know is that the Titanic wasn't even the flagship of this class. All in all, the Olympic class ships were marvels of sea engineering, but they seemed cursed to suffer disastrous fates.
paragraphs.translationZh: 您可能知道泰坦尼克号，但它实际上只是当时三艘最先进的远洋船舶之一。奥林匹克级船舶由北爱尔兰的 Harland & Wolff 船舶制造商为白星航运公司建造。奥林匹克级包括奥林匹克号、不列颠尼克号和泰坦尼克号。您可能不知道的是，泰坦尼克号甚至不是该级别的旗舰。总而言之，奥林匹克级船舶是海洋工程的奇迹，但它们似乎注定要遭受灾难性的命运。

paragraphs.sourceText: The Olympic launched first in 1910, followed by the Titanic in 1911, and lastly the Britannic in 1914. The ships had nine decks, and White Star Line decided to focus on making them the most luxurious ships on the water.
paragraphs.translationZh: 奥林匹克号于 1910 年首次下水，泰坦尼克号于 1911 年下水，最后是不列颠尼克号于 1914 年下水。这些船有九层甲板，白星航运公司决定专注于使它们成为水上最豪华的船舶。

paragraphs.sourceText: Stretching 269.13 meters, the Olympic class ships were wonders of naval technology, and everyone thought that they would continue to be so for quite some time. However, all suffered
paragraphs.translationZh: 奥林匹克级舰艇全长 269.13 米，是海军技术的奇迹，每个人都认为它们会在相当长的一段时间内保持这种状态。然而，所有人都遭受了

paragraphs.sourceText: terrible accidents on the open seas. The Olympic got wrecked before the Titanic did, but it was the only one to survive and maintain a successful career of 24 years. The Titanic was the first to sink after famously hitting a huge iceberg in 1912. Following this disaster, the Britannic hit a naval mine in 1916 and subsequently sank as well.
paragraphs.translationZh: 公海发生的可怕事故。奥林匹克号先于泰坦尼克号失事，但它是唯一一艘幸存并保持了 24 年成功职业生涯的船只。泰坦尼克号在 1912 年撞上巨大冰山后成为第一艘沉没的船只。这场灾难之后，英国号于 1916 年触雷，随后也沉没。

paragraphs.sourceText: Each ship was coal-powered by several boilers constantly kept running by exhausted crews below deck. Most recognizable of the ship designs are the ship's smoke stacks, but the fourth stack was actually just artistic in nature and served no functional purpose. While two of these ships sank, they were all designed with double hulls (船体) believed to make them "unsinkable", perhaps a mistaken idea that led to the Titanic's and the Britannic's tragic end.
paragraphs.translationZh: 每艘船都由几台锅炉提供煤炭动力，甲板下精疲力竭的船员不断地维持着这些锅炉的运转。最知名的船舶设计是船舶的烟囱，但第四个烟囱实际上只是艺术性的，没有任何功能性目的。虽然其中两艘船沉没，但它们都设计有双壳（船体），据信使它们“不沉”，也许是一个错误的想法导致了泰坦尼克号和不列颠尼克号的悲惨结局。

paragraphs.sourceText: The Olympic suffered two crashes with other ships and went on to serve as a hospital ship and troop transport in World War I. Eventually, she was taken out of service in 1935, ending the era of the luxurious Olympic class ocean liners.
paragraphs.translationZh: 奥林匹克号曾两次与其他船只相撞，随后在第一次世界大战中用作医院船和部队运输船。最终，她于 1935 年退役，结束了豪华奥林匹克级远洋客轮的时代。
